correctness.rationale: Constructed PG(2,4) in GF(4) by homogeneous coordinates; both independent programs exhaust all 2^21 point masks and all one/two swaps. Python additionally verifies all five incidence-preserving generators and checks their orbits exhaust all three static types, making BFS from one state per class sufficient for global eccentricities. Python and C++17 agree on counts 11480, degree types, 281 components, 90720 edges, radius/diameter 8 of mobile component, and full two-swap connectivity with radius 4/diameter 5. Cartesian-product corollary follows from independent 12-point shore bounds. Boundaries: no assertion beyond the specified plane and exchange rules.

The complete exchange graph, 280 frozen Hermitian-complement states, sharp two-exchange connectivity and distances are not stated in the inspected primary texts. Closest indexed published-finding corpus exchange problems concern single blocking sets in PG(2,3) or PG(2,4) hyperovals; neither has the same feasible family or adjacency relation. Priority remains qualified by historical access limits; a failed search alone is not proof.

value.rationale: A natural finite incidence design with a known nontrivial three-type optimum classification exhibits a striking qualitative separation between 280 rigid Hermitian-complement states and a large mobile sector. The sharp simultaneous-exchange budget two and exact graph radii/diameters have significance for feasibility-preserving relocation of strong transversals and double-total dominators, and provide a geometric obstruction not visible from static minimum size or orbit counts alone. This is a complete classification of a motivated finite optimization solution space, not an arbitrary slice or an incremental score.
